title: Mock 2 · PMS Rulebook
blurb: Registration, operations and fees with a high water mark caselet.

questions.q: In an Offer for Sale (OFS), the proceeds of the sale go to:
options: The company, increasing its share capital
Both the company and the promoters equally
The selling shareholders, with no increase in the company's share capital
The stock exchange's investor protection fund
questions.explanation: Section 2.2.1: an OFS does not increase share capital; proceeds go to the offerors (promoters or large investors).
hints: OFS involves no fresh issue by the company.
Correct: existing shareholders sell already-allotted shares.

questions.q: A stock trades at a P/E of 30 and its EPS is expected to grow at 20% a year. Using the PEG thumb rule, the stock appears:
options: Fairly valued, with a PEG of 1.0
questions.explanation: PEG = P/E ÷ growth = 30/20 = 1.5. PEG > 1 indicates overvaluation (Section 3.4).

questions.q: Which statement about bond price volatility is correct?
options: For the same maturity and yield change, a lower-coupon bond shows a larger percentage price change
Higher-coupon bonds are more volatile than lower-coupon bonds
Bond prices and interest rates move in the same direction
Equal increases and decreases in yield produce symmetrical price changes
questions.explanation: Section 4.5: bond price volatility is inversely related to coupon; zero-coupon bonds show the largest percentage change.
hints: Correct: volatility is inversely related to coupon.
A yield fall raises prices more than an equal rise lowers them.

questions.q: SEBI has mandated which settlement method for individual stock derivatives?
options: Physical settlement by delivery of the underlying stock
Settlement in the commodity futures contract
questions.explanation: Section 5.6: SEBI mandated physical settlement for all individual stock derivatives and commodity derivatives; index derivatives are cash settled.
hints: Index derivatives are cash settled, not stock derivatives.
That is how commodity options devolve.

questions.q: Which return measure must a portfolio manager use when communicating the performance of an investment approach, as it removes the effect of client cash flows?
options: Holding period return on the first investment only
questions.explanation: Sections 20.2.2 and 20.7: PMs present TWRR of the investment approach with the benchmark's trailing return; TWRR removes the effect of external cash flows.
hints: IRR depends on the timing of client flows; XIRR is used for the individual investor's report.
Correct: mandated by SEBI and GIPS.

questions.q: Except for a portfolio manager providing only advisory services, every portfolio manager must appoint a:
options: Custodian for the securities managed or administered by it
questions.explanation: Section 7.6.4: except for advisory-only PMs, every portfolio manager shall appoint a custodian.
hints: Not a regulatory requirement for PMs.

questions.q: A client redeems part of her PMS portfolio 20 months after investing. What is the maximum exit load the portfolio manager can charge on the amount redeemed?
questions.explanation: SEBI circular 13 February 2020: max 3% in year 1, 2% in year 2, 1% in year 3, nil after 3 years.
hints: 3% applies only in the first year.
Nil applies only after three years.

questions.q: Which of the following is a requirement for the Principal Officer of a portfolio manager?
options: At least 2 years' experience and graduation only
At least 10 years' experience in banking
At least 5 years' experience in related securities market activities, along with the relevant NISM certification
questions.explanation: Section 7.4: Principal Officer needs a professional qualification, 5 years' experience (with at least 2 in PM/IA/fund management) and the NISM certification.
hints: That describes the additional employee requirement.
CFA is one of several acceptable qualifications, not compulsory.

questions.q: Which of the following entities is NOT listed in the workbook as eligible to invest in PMS?
questions.explanation: Section 8.1 lists individuals, NRIs, HUFs, proprietorships, AOPs, partnership firms, LLPs, trusts and body corporates.
hints: Correct: not in the list of eligible entities.

questions.q: The disclosure document must be provided to a prospective PMS client:
options: At least two days before signing the agreement
Along with the account opening form, before or at the time of entering into the agreement
Within 30 days after signing the agreement
Only if the client asks for it
questions.explanation: Section 8.2: the disclosure document is given with the account opening form prior to/at signing and is available on the PM's website.
hints: That was the old rule, discontinued in 2020.
Correct: the 2020 regulations dropped the two-day rule.
Too late; it must be before or at signing.

questions.q: Which BB&K investor personality is confident and careful, likes doing own research and is often contrarian?
questions.explanation: Section 9.3.8: Individualists are confident, methodical and analytical, avoid extreme volatility and are often contrarian.

questions.q: Tactical asset allocation is best described as:
options: The long-term target policy portfolio derived from the IPS
Allocation decided solely by the client's tax bracket
A short-term deviation from the policy mix to exploit market opportunities ('timing the market')
questions.explanation: Section 9.5: SAA involves 'time in the market'; TAA is short-term and attempts 'timing the markets'.
hints: Tax is one constraint, not the definition.

questions.q: For an Indian company, residential status for income tax purposes is:
options: Resident only if its Place of Effective Management is in India
Non-resident if controlled from outside India
Determined by the residence of its directors
questions.explanation: Section 10.1.1.3: Indian companies are always treated as resident in India.
hints: Correct: an Indian company can never be non-resident.
Even subsidiaries controlled from abroad are resident.

questions.q: A portfolio manager offering non-discretionary services may invest up to what share of the client's AUM in unlisted securities (for clients other than large value accredited investors)?
questions.explanation: Section 11.4: non-discretionary or advisory PMs may invest/advise up to 25% of AUM in unlisted securities.
hints: Not the limit in the regulation.
100% is only for large value accredited investors.

questions.q: Under the PMS code of conduct, a portfolio manager shall:
options: Make statements about its superior capabilities to attract clients
Share clients' confidential information with the press when asked
Execute trades against client interest in its proprietary account if profitable
Not place its own interest above those of its clients
questions.explanation: Schedule III code of conduct: avoid conflicts, never place own interest above clients'.
hints: Confidential information must not be disclosed.

questions.q: An equal-weighted index has four stocks whose prices change by +10%, -5%, +20% and +15% over a day. If the index was at 1,000, its new level is about:
questions.explanation: Equal-weighted index moves by the arithmetic mean of percentage changes (Section 12.3.3): 10%.

questions.q: Operational efficiency of a market refers to:
options: How fully prices reflect all available information
How quickly insider information becomes public
How low the cost of transacting is
questions.explanation: Section 13.1: operational efficiency measures the cost of transacting.

questions.q: According to Prospect Theory, investors are generally:
options: Risk-seeking about gains and risk-averse about losses
Equally sensitive to gains and losses
Risk-averse about gains and risk-seeking about losses
questions.explanation: Section 14.2.2: people are risk-averse about gains and risk-seeking about losses; monetary losses hurt more.
hints: Losses hurt more than gains please.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly lists the four ways of treating an identified risk?
questions.explanation: Section 17.2: treatment of risk: (i) tolerate, (ii) mitigate, (iii) transfer, (iv) terminate.
hints: These are steps of the process, not treatment options.

questions.q: To identify VALUE stocks, which screen would a portfolio manager typically use?
questions.explanation: Section 18.8.2.1: value screens include low P/E, low PEG, low P/B, low P/S, low P/CF, high dividend yield, low D/E.
hints: Value screens look for HIGH dividend yield.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a passive fixed income strategy?
options: Barbell strategy based on a view of uncertain rate moves
questions.explanation: Section 19.2: the three passive strategies are buy and hold, indexing and immunization; barbell is active (19.3.1).
hints: Correct: barbell is an active interest-rate strategy.

questions.q: A balanced portfolio has a 60% target in equity with trigger points at 50% and 70%. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Section 21.3.1: threshold rebalancing sets trigger points such as 50% and 70% around a 60% target.
hints: Calendar rebalancing is by fixed dates.
Buy and hold does not rebalance.
CPPI uses a floor and multiplier.

questions.q: What performance fee is payable for Year 1?
questions.explanation: Year 1 gain above the starting value of ₹1 crore = ₹30 lakh; fee = 20% x 30 lakh = ₹6 lakh. HWM becomes ₹1.30 crore.
hints: That is the gain, not the fee.
There is a gain above the initial value.
questions.case: Mr. Kapoor invested ₹1 crore with a discretionary portfolio manager. The agreement provides a performance fee of 20% of gains above the high water mark (no hurdle rate, for simplicity). The pre-performance-fee portfolio values at the end of each year were: Year 1 ₹1.30 crore, Year 2 ₹1.15 crore, Year 3 ₹1.45 crore. As in the workbook illustration, the high water mark for the next period is the highest pre-fee closing value achieved so far.

questions.q: What performance fee is payable for Year 2?
questions.explanation: Pre-fee value ₹1.15 crore is below the high water mark of ₹1.30 crore, so no performance fee is payable.
hints: Value (1.15) is below the HWM (1.30): no fee.
questions.case: Mr. Kapoor invested ₹1 crore with a discretionary portfolio manager. The agreement provides a performance fee of 20% of gains above the high water mark (no hurdle rate, for simplicity). The pre-performance-fee portfolio values at the end of each year were: Year 1 ₹1.30 crore, Year 2 ₹1.15 crore, Year 3 ₹1.45 crore. As in the workbook illustration, the high water mark for the next period is the highest pre-fee closing value achieved so far.

questions.q: What performance fee is payable for Year 3?
questions.explanation: Fee only on value above the previous HWM of ₹1.30 crore: 20% x ₹15 lakh = ₹3 lakh (not on the full ₹30 lakh rise from ₹1.15 crore).
hints: Charges on the full rise from 1.15 crore.
Value exceeds the HWM, so a fee is due.
